# Preparing a legal manuscript

Start with an outline and assign a unique number to every chapter and section. Record the jurisdiction and date at which the law has been checked. Keep a separate register of cases, legislation and secondary authorities.

::: {.callout-note title="Editorial checkpoint"}
A citation appearing in a manuscript does not prove its accuracy. Read the underlying judgment, legislation or publication before accepting its proposition.
:::

# Reviewing authorities

For each authority, record the full citation, relevant page or paragraph, proposition supported, source location and verification date. Distinguish binding decisions from persuasive authorities.

## Case brief template

| Field | What to record |
|---|---|
| Citation | Court, parties, case number and date |
| Facts | Material facts relevant to the legal issue |
| Issue | Question determined by the court |
| Holding | Decision and applicable legal reasoning |
| Pinpoint | Page or paragraph supporting the proposition |

# Checking Word documents

The included Python utility reads DOCX files locally and reports duplicated typed heading numbers and unresolved footnote references. Run:

```bash
python audit.py manuscript.docx
```

The report identifies findings for human review. Automatic heading numbering through Word numbering definitions is not currently analysed.

# Producing an edition

Use Quarto to generate HTML, PDF and EPUB from a single source. Install Quarto and its PDF engine, then run:

```bash
quarto render book.qmd --to all
```

Inspect each output before distribution. Check page breaks, footnotes, tables, navigation and accessibility.

# Further reading

The official Quarto project guide explains project configuration and rendering.^[Quarto, Project Basics, https://quarto.org/docs/projects/quarto-projects.html.]

The GitHub Actions workflow in this repository runs tests, checks publication outputs and stores generated artifacts for inspection.
